## What

A browser audit of the store's product page for a buyer (274 [AX1]), in every state a buyer meets, found four causes short of WCAG 2.2 AAA. Each now has a permanent check (`tests/product-page-accessibility.test.ts`) and a minimal fix at its cause. No creator text or colour choice, price, limit, commission, flag or gate changes.

| Criterion | Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.4.6 Contrast (enhanced) | "3 left", "Sold out", "Coming soon" and any text in the creator's colour (`--st-accent-text`) | Derived to 4.5:1 only. With the default violet, axe measured 6.56:1 (#5a36ee on #ffffff, 14 px bold). This failed on the limited and sold-out states at every width and mode. | `lib/store-look.ts` derives it to 7:1 on the card, an item and the page. It moves only as far as it must, towards the page's own text. Default violet: light #5232d7 at 7.51:1, sand 8.33:1, night #b1a0f8 at 7.79:1. |
| 2.5.5 Target size (enhanced) | Boxes on the free form, the waitlist, the news, links and reminder boxes | Labels 20 px tall at 1280 px (40 px at 320 px) | `min-h-11`: at least 44 px |
| 2.5.5 | The rating link "4.5 (2)" | 24 px tall | `a.rv-line` min-height 2.75rem |
| 2.5.5 | "Everything from …" (product page), "Back to …" (reviews page and a call's booking page) | 18 px tall, a standalone link, not in a sentence | `inline-flex min-h-11 items-center` |
| 1.4.8 Visual presentation (line length) | The platform's own notes in the buy box: access, terms, payment, the closing sentence, the free-delivery note and the review rules | 86–115 letters a line at 1280 px and at 200% | `.st-measure` caps `p, li, dd, blockquote, figcaption` at 56ch on the product, reviews and booking pages. It uses `:where`, so it adds no specificity, and centered lines stay centered. 72ch still held 92–101 letters a line; 56ch holds 78 at most (0 lines over 80 across all cases). |
| 1.3.1 / 2.4.10 Headings | `/@store/p/<product>/reviews` | No h1 (axe `page-has-heading-one`) | `ReviewsSection` takes `level={1}` there and stays an h2 inside the product page |

Product files touched: `lib/store-look.ts`, `app/globals.css`, `components/store-product.tsx`, `components/assistant-reminder-box.tsx`, `components/review-list.tsx`, `app/[handle]/p/[product]/page.tsx`, `app/[handle]/p/[product]/reviews/page.tsx` and `app/[handle]/book/[product]/page.tsx`.

`--st-accent-text`, `components/store-product.tsx` and the two box labels are shared with the store page, which uses the same components. The store page gets the same contrast and target size there. Its own remaining items are listed below and are not fixed here.

## Proof

  - text spacing (1.4.12) at 320 and 1280 px;
  - 200% zoom (640 CSS px at DPR 2);

Each case ran axe-core 4.13 with the `wcag2a`…`wcag22aaa` and `best-practice` tags, plus geometry checks. The keyboard check was real Tab presses through the page: every focus was `:focus-visible`, in view, and had an outline of at least 2 px.

- **Criteria checked:**

Get it again" 18 px, and "Report a problem with this page" and "Delete my data from this store" 16 px. That page belongs to the store page's audit.

title: fix(a11y): booked-call links on the orders list name their call (AX274 2.4.9, by reference)
body:
Stacked on #2893

## What

WCAG 2.4.9 (Link Purpose, Link Only, AAA) on the buyer's list of purchases (`/@<store>/orders`, `app/[handle]/orders/page.tsx`). When a buyer has several booked calls, each call's "Join the call", "Add it to your calendar" and "Move it to another time" had the same words as every other call's. A screen reader's list of links showed nine links that could not be told apart.

Each of those links now gets its name by reference (technique ARIA7, `aria-labelledby`). The name is the card's heading (the product), then the call's time if the buyer booked the same product more than once, then the link's own words:

| Call | Old accessible name | New accessible name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Portfolio review", booked once | Add it to your calendar | Portfolio review Add it to your calendar |
| "Coaching call", booked twice | Add it to your calendar | Coaching call Thursday, November 12 at 3:00 PM Add it to your calendar |

**The visible words do not change in any language.** `lib/buyer-words/orders.ts` is not touched:

| Language | Join (other room) | Calendar | Move | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| en | Join the call | Add it to your calendar | Move it to another time | none (named by reference) |
| es | Unirse a la llamada | Añadirla a tu calendario | Cambiarla a otra hora | none |
| fr | Rejoindre l'appel | L'ajouter à votre agenda | Le déplacer à un autre horaire | none |
| de | Am Gespräch teilnehmen | Zu Ihrem Kalender hinzufügen | Auf eine andere Zeit verschieben | none |
| it | Partecipa alla chiamata | Aggiungila al tuo calendario | Spostala a un altro orario | none |
| nl | Deelnemen aan het gesprek | Zet het in je agenda | Verplaats het naar een ander tijdstip | none |
| pt | Entrar na chamada | Adicionar ao seu calendário | Mudar para outro horário | none |

**Why not visible wording like "Add “<product>” to your calendar".** The page has a byte bound tied to its cost meter: `ORDERS_PAGE_BYTES` (6,100,000) feeds `ORDERS_OPEN_READ` and `ORDERS_OPEN_UNITS`. Before this change, the worst page measured 6,082,873 bytes, which left 17,127. The worst case is `MAX_LISTED` = 40 calls with an 80-character title made of "&", which costs 11 bytes per character between the HTML and the payload. Putting the title in just two of the links would add about 40 × 2 × 80 × 11 ≈ 70 KB, so it would break the bound. Raising the bound would change the cost of opening the page, which is an MR decision outside this PR. Naming by reference adds a fixed number of bytes per call, whatever the title's length.

Other repeated link texts checked:
- "Review <product>", "Open <product>", "Download <product>", "Show the products in <product>" and "Your license key for <product>" already name the product.
- **Still failing 2.4.9, not fixed here:** "Renew your membership", "Book a session (N left)", "Add the podcast to your app" and "Review what you bought" (an order with several products). They repeat when two purchases share the same shape. Naming them by reference too would add about 8 KB in the worst case (the podcast shape, 40 cards), which is more than the 2,767 bytes left. They need room in `ORDERS_PAGE_BYTES` first.

## Proof

- RED `5dd4392ec`: `tests/orders-accessibility.test.ts` gets a new case with three booked calls, two of one product. It checks that every link on the page has an accessible name that no other link has, that each name contains the words the link shows, and that each call's three links name its product. Result: 3 tests, 2 pass, 1 fail. Nine links had repeated names.
- GREEN `87eec44fc`: 3 / 3 pass.
- `tests/orders-page-bounds.test.ts`: 21 / 21 pass. The worst page is now 6,097,233 bytes (podcast, keys taken back, fr), up from 6,082,873 and under 6,100,000.
- Tests that import or read the touched files, all passing: buyer-waiting (33), call-place-pages (21), cart-course (17), course-link-delivery-copy (30), email-fields (48), license-key-faq (18), orders-link-copy (38), orders-open (34), store-language (980), thanks-note (14), traffic (75), plan-cost-registry (24), orders-accessibility (3).
- eslint is clean on both files. `tsc --noEmit` reports nothing for them. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Synthetic records and a stand-in Stripe only. No price, limit, commission, flag or gate changes.

## Acessibilidade

- **2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only), AAA:** checked by computing accessible names in the test (accname: `aria-labelledby`, then `aria-label`, then content) over the server-rendered page. With three calls, every link's name is unique and names its call. The only links fixed are the booked calls' links. The four repeated purchase-card links listed above still fail and are recorded as a gap.
- **2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context), AA:** still met. The name now carries the context by itself.
- **2.5.3 Label in Name:** the test checks that each link's name contains its visible words.
- **3.1.5 Reading Level:** the visible words are unchanged. The added part of each name is the product's title and the time already shown on the card.
- **Method:** automated rendering of the real page and component with synthetic data. **Exclusions:** no screen-reader run (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), no voice-control check, and no tests with people (item 202). These remain gaps, not passes.
- **Steps and decisions for the main task:** 0 → 0 (no new interaction).

title: Security: a visitor's utm_source can no longer break a store page or write onto Object.prototype through the stats sums (rule 30)
body:
This is the rule 30 follow-up to #2856. In each site below, a key a visitor (or the creator's own Stripe metadata) can choose was added up or looked up on a plain object, so `__proto__` or `constructor` wrote onto, or read from, the shared prototype.

## The worst cases (each proven by a RED test)
- **`lib/source-rules.ts` `sourceAlias`:** `sourceAlias("constructor")` returned `[Function: Object]`. Through `proxy.ts` `touchFrom`, **any `/@handle?utm_source=constructor` link broke that store page for every visitor** (a middleware error). The hit route also threw, and the checkout channel metadata was lost.
- **`lib/stats.ts`, on the visitor's utm:**
  - `renewalsFrom` (:1198) and `channelDays` (:1625) wrote `Object.prototype["<day>"] = cents` **for the whole server process**;
  - `byProduct` (:1518) made `readSales` throw;
  - `refundsByProduct` (:1617) and the all-time `byProduct` (:1911) wrote `Object.prototype.sales` and `.cents` as NaN.
- **The studio home** (`resultsByCampaign`, formerly the inline reduce): `__proto__` replaced the record's prototype, and the sums came out NaN.
- **The weekly e-mail:** it named the channel `function Object()…`.
- **`also-bought` / `next-bought`:** an array was set as the prototype, and counts became `'function Object() {…}111'`.

## The change
- The sums are done in `Object.create(null)` or a Map and handed on as `{ ...acc }` or `Object.fromEntries`, so pages still receive an ordinary object. A null-prototype object passed to a Client Component throws in production, so the hand-on is always a plain object.
- `sourceAlias` and `channelWord` use `Object.hasOwn`.
- The studio's short-links reduce moves word for word into `resultsByCampaign` (lib/stats.ts), so a test can reach it. `app/studio/page.tsx` changes by one hunk plus the import.

## Tests
- `tests/proto-keys.test.ts` is new.
  - RED 53ec7c58: 5 of 8 fail. Fix 935bbcc4.
  - RED 7d04f0e6: 6 of 15 fail. Fix def87c72: 15 of 15.
- The tests also check that whatever reaches a page is an ordinary object.
- **165 files** pass: the 99 that import lib/stats, the 63 that read app/studio/page, and the importers of stats-report, source-rules, also-bought and next-bought.
- eslint and tsc are clean, and client-bundles reports 0 failures. No existing test changed.

## Held by others (patch offered, not here)
Branch `claude4/proto-keys-held-offer` @ a06d773a, for Claude 3 (#2571, #1924):
- `lib/page-depth.ts`: a visitor's block id `constructor` wrote `Object.played`;
- `lib/partner-share.ts` and the affiliates route: a 500 for the creator;
- `components/stats-panel.tsx`: should use `sourceName()`.

## Cost (MR)
None.

## Acessibilidade
No interface change. The studio page renders the same object as before.

title: fix(a11y): page editor targets, focus, announcements and layout shift (AX274 2.5.5, 2.4.3, 4.1.3, 1.4.10, 2.2.5)
body:
Page editor accessibility: focus kept on block moves, removals and saves; 44 px targets; no layout shift at 1280

Branch `claude6/a11y-page-editor`. Scope: `/studio/pages?product=<id>` and `components/page-editor.tsx` with the block editors it draws. Not touched: the page-read lines in `app/studio/pages/page.tsx` (#2832), `readThanksNote` (:264), the `page_unread` messages (#2830). No open PR touches `components/page-editor.tsx`, `components/page-style-picker.tsx`, `components/saved-sections.tsx` or `lib/block-insert.ts`.

## What

Each finding was seen in Chromium on a production build with synthetic data (the e2e fakes and the store-copy seed). Before and after are measured with the same scratch audit.

1. **Targets under 44 × 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5).** Before: each block's Move up, Move down, Duplicate and Remove buttons were 40 × 40. Inside block panels, a list's Remove item and a comparison table's yes/no cells were 40 × 40. A step's, a question's, a row's, a quotation's and a picture's buttons were 36 × 36. "Earlier versions", "Saved sections" and "Search and sharing" opened from a line 20–24 px high. After: every one is at least 44 × 44, and the summaries are 44–48 px high with no visual move (`-my-3 py-3`). After the fix the audit finds no editor control under 44 px at 320, 390, 640 (200%), 1280 or 320 at DPR 4 (400%), in the empty and filled states, in every block panel, or in a newly added Text, Video, Pictures or Button block. The only exception left is "Ask on my sales pages", a button inside a sentence (2.5.5 inline exception).
2. **A block's name was squeezed to 12 px at 320 px and at 400% zoom (WCAG 1.4.10, 2.5.5).** Before: the name button, which opens the block, was 12 × 56 px beside the four action buttons. After: the row wraps its buttons under the name when there is no room, and the name keeps at least 9rem.
3. **Focus lost to `<body>` (WCAG 2.4.3).**
   - **Move:** before, moving a block to the last place it can take turned its button off (`disabled`) under the focus. After, the button stays focusable with `aria-disabled`, and further presses do nothing.
   - **Remove:** before, the row went away with the focus in it. After, the focus moves to the block now in its place, or the one before it, or the place to add a block when none is left (`focusAfterRemoval`).
   - **Save:** before, Save turned itself off while saving, so the focus fell to the body on success, on a refusal ("could not be read", signed out) and on a network error. After, Save stays focusable (`aria-disabled`), and a press while it cannot save does nothing.
   - **Pictures:** the "Move picture earlier/later" buttons also stay focusable at the ends.
4. **Moves and removals were silent (WCAG 4.1.3, 3.3.6).** After a move, the status region now says "Moved How it works to position 7 of 7." After a removal it says "Removed Benefits from position 2. Undo, at the top of the editor, brings it back." Undo (button and Ctrl+Z) was checked to bring the block back.
5. **The choice that is on was told apart by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1, 1.4.11, forced colors).** This applied to Build or Preview, a block's "Shows on" and the page style. Before, with forced colors on, the pressed and unpressed buttons had identical computed styles. After, a check is shown beside the one that is on, as the editor's other switches (Computer/Phone, Add blocks/Preview) already do. A screenshot under forced colors shows "Build ✓" and "Preview ✓".
6. **Layout shift at 1280 (CLS 0.0895).** The editor was drawn in one column and switched to two by script after hydration (`matchMedia`). That narrowed the column of blocks from 856 to 426 px and pushed "Translate the whole page" and the version test below the fold. After, the two columns come from the style sheet at the same `min-width: 1280px`. The saved sections under the blocks are hidden by CSS at that width until the script moves them beside. Measured CLS, median of 3 runs on an emulated slow network: 1280 px went from 0.0895 to 0.0016, 1440 px from 0.0893 to 0.0068, and 390 px stayed at 0. The residual is "Write the whole page with AI" moving when a part above it finishes loading on the client.
7. **Session ended (WCAG 2.2.5).** Before, a save refused with `signed_out` said "Your session ended. Log in again."; signing in in the same tab leaves the page this tab still holds. After, it says: "Your session ended. Your changes are still here, not saved yet: sign in again in a new tab, then come back to this tab and press Save the page." It also has a 44 px link, "Sign in again in a new tab", which opens `/signin` in a new tab.

Product files touched: `components/page-editor.tsx`, `components/page-style-picker.tsx`, `components/saved-sections.tsx`, `lib/block-insert.ts` (`movedSaying`, `removedSaying`, `focusAfterRemoval`). Tests updated to the new markup, with the same meaning: `tests/block-insert.test.ts`, `tests/feature-visual-cards.test.ts`, `tests/side-panel.test.ts`.

No price, limit, commission, flag, gate or creator content is changed.

## Proof

- RED `810fbb5fb`, new test `tests/page-editor-block-actions-a11y.test.ts`: 26 of 28 checks fail.
- RED `59c3295a5` adds the 2.2.5 checks. Run against the unfixed code, 28 of 30 checks fail. This commit also corrects two anchors of the first RED:
  - `\bdisabled=` also matched `aria-disabled=`; it is now `(?<[-\w])disabled=`;
  - the grid check now reads the build view's own grid.
- GREEN `28cb47156`: 30 of 30 pass. The 23 test files that read the touched files pass, 918 checks in total.
- `eslint` passes on the touched files, `git diff --check` is clean, and `next build` (including `tsc --noEmit`) passes.
- Browser audit (scratch, not committed), production build, Chromium 1 engine:

  | Check | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Moving a block down to the end | focus on body | focus stays on "Move block 7 down", status said |
  | Remove block 2 | focus on body, nothing said | focus on "2. Who it is for", status said |
  | Save: ok, `shape`, `signed_out`, network error | focus on body | focus on "Save the page"; "Page saved." in a polite live region, refusals in `role=alert` |
  | Tab walk through the editor (75 stops) | — | every stop `:focus-visible` with a 3 px solid outline, none clipped by an overflow edge |
  | CLS at 1280 | 0.0895 | 0.0016 |

- axe-core, with the wcag2a/aa/aaa, 21, 22 and best-practice tags (including `color-contrast-enhanced`), finds 0 violations both before and after in these cases:
  - empty and filled pages at 320, 390, 1280, 200% and 400% zoom;
  - text spacing at 390 and 1280;
  - reduced motion and forced colors at 1280 and 390;
  - every block panel open, at 1280 and 390.
- After the fix only (not run on the unfixed build), axe also finds 0 violations in these cases:
  - Text, Video, Pictures and Button blocks added;
  - Preview at 1280, 390 and 320.

## Acessibilidade

**Criteria checked.**
- WCAG 2.2 AAA: 1.4.1, 1.4.6 and 1.4.11 (axe enhanced contrast; non-color state), 1.4.10 (320 px and 400%), 1.4.12 (text spacing), 2.1.1 (keyboard only, including moving blocks without dragging, 2.5.7), 2.3.3 (reduced motion), 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11 and 2.4.13, 2.5.5, 3.3.6 (Undo after a removal), 3.3.7, 2.2.5 and 4.1.3.
- Forced colors.

title: PayPal: a payment written down whose reply was lost is handed over by the sweep, exactly once
body:
Stacked on #2854 (claude4/paypal-sales-exact). This is money: 2 reviews.

## The problem (it existed before, and #2854 made it reachable)
Two ways reach it:
- the SET of the paid record was applied, but its reply came back unknown;
- `redisPipeline` threw after Redis applied it.

Either way, the next sweep found the record with the order still pending, and `if (!opened || written) ZREM` took it off the watch **without handing over**. The buyer paid and received nothing.

## The change
- **`settledWrites(paid)`:** the seven writes that follow the record (refund watch, the buyer's orders, off pending, sales) now share one function. The commands are the same.
- **`captureOrder`:** any failure writing the payment down keeps the order pending (`watchLater`) and answers "error". Nothing is handed over on the return.
- **`watchPayPal`, pending orders:**
  - `readPaidExact`: unknown → stays pending; a missing opened record → off pending, as before.
  - A record that is already written no longer takes the order off the watch. PayPal is asked, as for any other order.
  - **Completed, with the record's store, product and capture matching:** the sweep **hands over first** and then makes the settled writes. A failed hand-over stays pending and is retried on the next pass.
  - Refunded, declined or voided: off pending, nothing is handed over. A record that does not match stays pending, with a log.

## Every hand-over step is idempotent (read in the code)
| Step | Why repeating it does nothing |
|---|---|
| `grantImported` | HSETNX, plus SADD for the buyers |
| `setPastBuyers` | a flag |
| `recordEnrollment` | HSETNX plus a cache DEL |
| Data-room charge (`orderWrite`) | the script charges only what is added (0 on a repeat) |
| Receipt | `idempotencyKey nimbus-paypal:<order>`, 24 h, "order" meter |
| `countOrder` | SET NX, 45 days |
| `creditPayPalSale` | HSETNX by `paypal:<order>`, by `ref:partner`, buyer bond |
| `emitEvent` | SET NX, 30 days |

**Why the receipt cannot repeat:** it goes out after the only steps that can throw (grant and enrollment), and everything after it swallows its own errors. A hand-over that failed therefore never sent the e-mail.

## Tests
- `tests/paypal-handover-exact.test.ts` is new. RED 32f08a43 fails 5 of 7 (never handed over, dropped from pending, or the return throwing). Fix 1766bf98: 7 of 7. It covers:
  - the reply lost or thrown after it was applied: exactly 1 hand-over;
  - an interrupted sweep;
  - a failure followed by a success: still 1;
  - PayPal unreachable: stays pending;
  - refunded: no hand-over;
  - a normal return: fresh once, and the sweep hands over nothing.
- `paypal-sales-exact` has one control adapted (rule 23): it encoded the old assumption.
- The 101 tests (paypal, person-copy, closing-buyers, mcp-tools, api-read, buyer-profile, g2791, plan-cost-registry) pass.
- eslint and tsc are clean, and client-bundles reports 0 failures.

## Cost (MR)
No new kind of command. The resume path costs one command less than a normal settle (no SET NX).

## Still open (next unit)
- **The return and the fresh sweep:** both take the order off pending **before** the hand-over, and a failure there leaves the buyer paid with nothing to retry. The fix is to hand over first, as the resume path does.
- **The sweep's seven-write pipeline:** if it applies the ZREM and then throws, the order is lost from pending.

title: Reviews (MR (c) part 1): at most 3 photo puts per review, granted in the review's own write before any put
body:
MR external-cost audit, unit (c) part 1, the choice Claude 4 approved in C4-20261106-2720-C5-160: "um limite de trocas de foto por avaliação, gravado no próprio registro da avaliação que já é escrito (zero comando novo)". The monthly cost line and its ceiling (photo weight 2 on the public figure, or a monthly counter) wait on Claude 4's choice. This bounds Blob spend, so it needs two reviews.

## The gap
`app/api/store/review/route.ts` put the buyer's photo to Vercel Blob BEFORE the words were saved. That is a paid Advanced Operation, retried up to 11 times by the SDK. The only ceilings were the public figure and 10 changes per order per hour, so one review could make many puts, including one before a write that then failed.

## What changed
- **`lib/review-summary.ts`:** `MAX_REVIEW_PHOTOS = 3`, and the `Review` record gets an optional `photoPuts`.
- **`lib/reviews.ts`:**
  - `parseReview` reads the counter strictly: absent is 0; a non-negative integer is capped at 3; any other value (text, negative, fraction, null) is 3, because unknown is never zero.
  - `SaveInput.photo` and `SaveResult.photoGranted`.
  - **The slot is granted inside `saveReview`,** which already runs under the product's lock (`takeLock`, the same as `creatorChange` and `setReviewPhoto`). The counter is read in the HGET and written in the HSET it already does: **no new command**. Two sends at once cannot both take the last slot.
- **`lib/review-photo.ts`:** `putReviewPhoto(ref, checked)` does only the put; `keepReviewPhoto` uses it.
- **`app/api/store/review/route.ts`,** new order:
  1. `checkReviewPhoto` checks the bytes, with no network.
  2. `saveReview` saves the words and grants the slot.
  3. The put happens only when the slot was granted.
  4. `setReviewPhoto` puts the photo on the review.
  - **No slot:** the words are saved, and the answer is `photoLimit`.
  - **A failed put after the grant:** the slot stays spent (fail closed for cost), and the answer is `photoFailed`. A failed `setReviewPhoto` after the put also answers `photoFailed`; before, it answered "saved" without the photo.
  - **Removing a photo** makes no put and takes no slot.
- **`lib/buyer-words/giving.ts`:** two sentences in all 7 languages, in `photoPaused`'s register. `photoPaused` ("this store is not taking new photos right now") would be false here, so it stays for the costs-paused case.
  - `photoLimit`: "Your review was saved, but the new photo was not added: a review can take 3 new photos in all, and yours has had 3."
  - `photoFailed`: "…because of a problem on our side. That try still counts as 1 of the 3 new photos a review can take."
- **`components/review-form.tsx`:** `photoLimit` is a status ("done"), and `photoFailed` an alert.

## Tests
- **RED `573d5b1c`:** `tests/review-photo-limit.test.ts` failed 27 of 41. It showed a put before a busy write (the photo then deleted), a 4th and a 5th put on one review, and no notice and no counter.
- **Fix `6a99e06e`:** 41/41.
- **31 test files pass:** the 26 that import reviews, review-photo, the route, review-summary, review-form or giving, plus store-data-registry, plan-cost-registry, person-data-registry and platform-us-english.
- eslint and `git diff --check` are clean, tsc shows no errors in the changed files, and check_public_data shows 0.
- The record's few extra bytes are already counted by `reviewBytes`.

## Gaps
- **A deleted and rewritten review starts at 0 again,** because its record is gone. That is still bounded by 10 changes per order per hour; closing it would need a marker kept for the deleted review.
- **A put that fails midway** may leave an orphan file in Blob, as before (MR item 3, `images/` storage, waits on Claude 4).
- **The form does not warn before the 4th try.**

## Acessibilidade
- The new sentences are plain, true, and name the number.
- They show in the form's existing live region: `role="status"` for the limit, `role="alert"` for the failure.
- German uses the formal Ihre register, checked in the test.
- No real screen reader was used.
- **Steps and decisions for the buyer:** 1 → 1 in the usual cases. At a 4th photo, the photo used to be saved with no limit; now the words are saved and a notice says why the photo was not added. No new decision.

title: Security: a buyer's utm_campaign can no longer write onto Object.prototype (email sales by tag)
body:
## The problem (security, found in an independent review of #2798; the code is older than that PR)
`moneyByCampaign` (lib/mail-revenue.ts) added up email sales on a plain `{}`, keyed by the campaign tag:

```ts
by[sale.campaign] ??= { sales: 0, cents: 0 }
```

**The buyer chooses that tag** through `utm_campaign`. `lib/came-from.ts` keeps `[a-z0-9._-]`, so `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` get through. The attack:
1. Anyone opens a store page with `?utm_source=email&utm_campaign=__proto__` and buys.
2. The next time the creator's email studio misses its cache, `Object.prototype.sales` and `Object.prototype.cents` are set **for the whole server process**, and every other `.sales` read in that process, for any store, is corrupted.

Reviewer's proof: `({}).sales = NaN`.

## The change
The record is created with `Object.create(null)`. Any tag, whatever its name, is only ever an own key, and no prototype is written. Nothing else changes.

Rule 23: tests/mail-links.test.ts compares the record by its own keys (`{ ...by }`), because a record with no prototype is not deep-equal to a literal `{}`.

## Before → after
1. **MEDIUM money, `readOpened` / `watchPayPal`.**
   - Before: a malformed or short GET counted as "record gone". The order was taken off the watch, and PayPal was never asked about it. If the capture went through, the buyer paid and received nothing.
   - After: only a confirmed GET null ends the watch. Anything else throws `UnknownReplyError`; the sweep logs it, keeps the order pending and moves to the next one.

3. **`readPayPalSales`.**
   - The envelope is exact; a non-list, more than limit+1 members, or an MGET without one slot per record throws.

4. **`paypalOrdersOf`:** exact. The person's copy fails as a whole instead of leaving PayPal orders out.
5. **`settle`:** only "OK" is fresh and only null is not fresh. Anything else throws before any hand-over: the order goes back on watch (`watchLater`), and the answer is "error".

title: Assignments: erasing a person deletes and counts every task record, even one that cannot be read; hand-in reads are exact (rule 24)
body:
This fixes a privacy MEDIUM and two LEVEs from the rule 24/30 sweep of Claude 4's modules (C4-2800).

## The problems
1. **MEDIUM, privacy, `forgetTasksPerson`:** a short or malformed GET reply, or a stored record that did not parse, was treated as "never handed in". Nothing was deleted, and the eraser reported `{records: 0, files: []}`, so the person was told they had been erased. Proven: 0 DELs.
2. **LEVE, `submissionOf`:** a malformed GET counted as "nothing handed in". The approved → closed gate (409) was skipped, so approved work was overwritten, `tries` was reset and the old file was orphaned.
3. **LEVE:**
   - `waitingWork` (`Array.isArray … : []`, `Number(total) || 0`) showed an empty queue;
   - `tellCreatorNow` (`fresh !== null`) let a malformed reply send an extra e-mail.

## The change
1. **Erasure:**
   - **A bad reply** (short, or a slot that is neither text nor nil): it throws `UnknownReplyError` before any deletion, and the erasure's retry finds everything in place.
   - **A stored record that cannot be read:** it is **still deleted**, and it is taken out of the waiting and all lists. The function then throws `TaskRecordUnreadError`, and `lib/person-erasure.ts` reports `incomplete`, never "done".
   - **The files of the readable records in that case:** they go into `nl:tasks:doors` with score 0, the same fallback the erasure already uses. The daily cron deletes them and gives the room back.
   - **The answer to the DEL itself:** left unchecked on purpose. Throwing there would lose the paths of files that were most likely already deleted, which would be worse for privacy.
2. **`submissionOf`:** only nil is "nothing handed in". Any other reply, or a record not in the shape `handIn` and `review` write, throws.
   - The POST of `course/task/route.ts` (not edited) turns the throw into a 500 before writing anything; the test proves the record stays untouched.
   - The lesson page and the studio page go to `app/error.tsx`, the same honest state as an unreadable quiz attempt.
3. **The two LEVEs:**
   - `waitingWork` reads exact pairs (`lesson|who`, whole-second scores) and an exact ZCARD;
   - `tellCreatorNow`: "OK" means tell now, nil means already told this hour, and anything else throws. Its caller already catches and logs.

- `tests/assignment-reads-exact.test.ts` is new. RED 645d7e59 fails 25 of 30; only the 5 controls pass. Fix 1224a5d3: 29 of 29 pass. The fix drops the RED test about the DEL answer, for the privacy reason given above.

No new round trips. There is one `ZADD` to doors inside the existing delete pipeline, and only when a record cannot be read. Nothing in plan-cost-registry counts these functions.

That allowed 24 pictures per save across 2,000 studio requests a month on Creator, which is 48,000 checks. With the read counted whole, that comes to about US$ 5 a month, past the owner's US$ 66 for a refunded first year.

  - The folder and ownership checks stay first; they cost nothing.
  - Then the claim, and the Blob check only for the pictures **this save took from the picture door**, each checked once.
  - A picture taken by an earlier save was checked then, so a save tried again never asks Blob about it twice.
- **`lib/sales-page-store.ts` `claimNewPictures`:** a new optional `onTaken` callback says which paths this call took from the door. The signature and behavior are unchanged for every other caller. It touches only this function, nothing near `readPage`, which is in #1947/#2830.
- **`lib/picture-check.ts` `keptPictures`:** checks those taken pictures. Any that is not a picture is released by the page and deleted. It came from the door in this very save, so it is nobody else's file. No later save can then put it on unchecked.

`picture-uploads` (#2803) and `picture-thumbnails` (#2801) each multiplied the **whole** studio figure, but doors, attaches and page saves share it. Neither line counted the door's signed token. They become one line, **`studio-blob`**: `STORE_ALLOWANCES[tier].studio × studioBlobPerRequest()`.

Each request is counted at the dearest kind it may be:
- **A door:**
  - its put, with 11 tries;

I could not re-read vercel.com from this session; the prices are the ones Claude 4 read on 6 November 2026, and "Delete operations are free" is from Codex Z's reading.

title: PayPal: the refund list, its records and the kept counts are read exactly (rule 24/30)
body:
Stacked on #2809 (base `claude4/paypal-revoke-atomic`). This closes the LEVE from rule 30 that I left open in #2791.

## The problem
`readPayPalRefundsWithCoverage` and `paypalKept` in lib/paypal-sales.ts read three replies loosely. Each could pass a malformed reply on as a believable value:
- **The ZRANGEBYSCORE … WITHSCORES reply:** `Array.isArray`, then `Number(score) || 0`. A non-list, a list of odd length or a bad score became 0 or an empty list.
- **The MGET of the records:** a short or misaligned reply turned silently into "missing".
- **The two counts in `paypalKept` (`Number(x) || 0`):** a malformed ZCARD became 0, so the studio charged for zero PayPal sales before the full read. ZCARD answers 0 for a missing key and never null, so null is not a confirmed absence either.

- **ZRANGEBYSCORE:** read with `stringList(repliesFor(reply, 1)?.[0])`. The list must have even length and stay within `2 * (PAYPAL_REFUNDS_READ + 1)`, and every score must pass `REDIS_SCORE`; otherwise it throws `UnknownReplyError`. An empty list still means no refunds.
- **MGET:** one slot per record asked for, each text or null; otherwise it throws. A record that is text but not JSON still marks the read as partial, as before.
- **`paypalKept`:** `repliesFor(…, asked)` and `countOf`. It throws on a missing, short, extra, null, text, negative or fractional count. Refunds not asked for still count 0.
- **Callers:** none changed. Every caller already handles a throw, because `redisPipeline` could already throw:

- the door was already spent;
- the student was told the file was `missing`, which was false;
- a retry answered `invalid`, so the hand-in was lost;

4. The store answered "not there" (`null`) → `missing`, as before.

**Single use still holds.** `takeTaskUpload` is one atomic `ZREM`. Every side effect (deleting a wrong-type or too-big file, `takeRoom`, `handIn`) still comes after the door is won. title: Page reads: an unknown answer is never an empty page, and the studio refuses before writing from one (unit A)
body:
## What

Unit A of C4-20261106-2610-C6-153 (MEDIUM: truth, SEO, portability), from Codex T's proof (`codex/t-own-page-unknown-proof` `64b3a0a9`), which Revisor 2 reproduced in cycle 143.

**Stacked on solrenning-llc/marktmorgen#1947** (`claude3/aa2-landing-store`), which owns `lib/sales-page-store.ts`. The base moves to main once #1947 is merged. `app/api/store/product/route.ts` is not touched; it belongs to #1947 and then unit B.

### The readers (`lib/sales-page-store.ts`)

`readPage` and `readPages` used to turn any answer they did not understand into an empty page. They now take only exact answers (CX-123 rule 24):

| Redis answers | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET `null`, or MGET slots of `null` | empty page | empty page (no change) |
| a page's JSON | the page | the page |
| no reply, one reply too many, a slot that is not a text, a text that is not a page, a shorter MGET list | empty page | `UnknownReplyError` |
| the request itself fails | throws | throws (no change) |

`pageOf` reads a kept record through the existing `pageRecordExact`, already used by `readPageExact`. `readMany` checks each MGET with `repliesFor`, which requires exactly one slot per key.

### The routes that decide a write from that read

Each one now answers **503 `page_unread` before writing anything**, except `apply`, which answers `page_unread_counted` (see the table):

| Route | What was decided from an unknown read |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/store/page` (save) | The earlier page's pictures, which drive `lockedFor`, claims, releases and the version pushed. A page and its picture were saved as if nothing had been there. |
| `GET /api/store/page` (copy) | A copy started from an empty page. |
| `GET /api/store/page-versions?n=` | Which pictures a version brought back keeps. All were dropped. |
| `POST /api/store/site-page` (save) | Same as the product page's save. |
| `GET /api/store/saved-blocks?section=` | The pages that use a section were listed as none. |
| `POST /api/store/saved-blocks` `update` | The pages that use it are now read **before** the section is written. |
| `POST /api/store/saved-blocks` `apply` | The month's count is taken first, as on main. Then every page is read **before** any page is written. An unknown read writes no page and answers **503 `page_unread_counted`**, because its try was already counted. Before, it wrote pages from a false empty page. |

**Why `page_unread` and not `unavailable`.** The page editor already shows `unavailable` as "Stores are not switched on yet, so nothing was saved." (`components/page-editor.tsx:175`). So the new codes have their own words in `lib/studio-messages.ts`:
- `page_unread`: "A page could not be read just now, so nothing was changed. Reload, then try again."
- `page_unread_counted` (apply only): "A page could not be read just now, so no page was changed. This try still counts toward this month's section updates. Reload, then try again."

The page editor and the saved-sections panel already spread `STUDIO_MESSAGES`. The copy and the versions buttons already say "could not be read just now". No component changes.

### Cost (MR)

- **No Redis command is added on any path** compared with main.
- **Codex Z's review of `3fe66000`** (MEDIUM, `codex/z-review-2830-apply-read` `cc6a2e2b`) showed that reading the pages before the month's count made an `apply` past the figure read 123,216 page bytes, where its studio unit covers 50,000. The apply is back in main's order, so that refusal reads no page. A test case keeps this (credit: Codex Z).
- **One trade-off, said in words:** an apply whose page read is unknown keeps the one try it counted.
- **The `update` reads the pages that use the section before writing it.** Those are the same reads it already made after the write, so the only extra reads are when the section disappears in between (`gone`).
- The store-data and plan-cost registries pass unchanged.

## Proof

- **RED `81028c1c`:**
  - `tests/page-reads-exact.test.ts` (T's reader cases kept as a permanent test, with credit): 12 tests, 9 failing.
  - `tests/page-routes-unknown.test.ts` (the real routes with a real session; only the page read's answer changed, as "no reply" or "not a page"): 118 checks, 26 failing. On that commit the product page and the store page were saved without their pictures, a version was pushed, the section was rewritten and put on pages, and the month's count went up.
- **GREEN `3fe66000`:** 12/12 and 118/118. Each route, in both modes, answers `[503, "page_unread"]`, and these are byte-identical to before: the page records, the picture owners, the earlier versions, the section and its uses, the month's count, and the product's page flag. The healthy copy, version, section listing, save and apply still answer 200.
- **RED `b719d4ce`** (after Codex Z's review): 121 checks, 5 failing on `3fe66000`. The apply past the figure read pages, and the unknown apply did not say its try was counted.
- **GREEN `43d59820`:** 121/121. Past the figure: `[429, "applies_full"]` with 0 page reads. Unknown apply: `[503, "page_unread_counted"]`, exactly one try counted, and nothing else changed.
- **Linked tests:** 45 test files that import the store, the routes or the studio messages, plus `plan-cost-registry`, `store-data-registry`, `closing-families`, `funnel-share`, `saved-sections` and `platform-us-english`. 0 failing. `tests/partner-copy.test.ts` (the registry of `STUDIO_MESSAGES` keys) gains `page_unread` and `page_unread_counted`.
- `tsc` on the 8 files: 0 errors. eslint: 0. `git diff --check` is clean.
- **Not run:** the full suite, the browser matrices (left to CI), real Redis.

title: 588 [KB9]: the EU withdrawal function (Art. 11a): official reading, rules and the buyer's function on /orders
body:
Queue item 588 [KB9]: the "withdraw from contract here" function required by Directive 2011/83/EU Art. 11a, applied from 19 June 2026. No price, limit, commission, flag or gate changes.

## Reading (`docs/kb9-eu-withdrawal-2026-11-06.md`)

Directive (EU) 2023/2673, OJ L 2023/2673 of 28.11.2023, was read on 6 November 2026 from the Publications Office's Cellar; the SHA-256 is recorded. EUR-Lex answered every request with a browser challenge, and that challenge was not bypassed. The document has Art. 11a verbatim, Art. 6(1)(h), Annex I and Art. 2's dates.

Owner's decisions (C4-20261106-2640-DONO-156):
- A buyer of a Marktmorgen plan counts as a consumer.
- A membership's withdrawal only tells the creator. Nothing writes to the creator's Stripe.

## Unit 1a: rules (`lib/withdrawal-rules.ts`)

When the function is offered, by kind of purchase:

| Kind of purchase | Offered |
| --- | --- |
| Any purchase, by default | 14 days from the contract |
| Digital content with the art. 16(m) yes | Not once supplied |
| Pre-order not yet handed over | 14 days; its planned release day ends nothing (only real supply does) |
| Membership | 14 days |
| Brought over from another platform, or given by the creator | Never |
| Shipped item | No end while its receipt is not known (its 14 days run from receipt) |
| Time that cannot be read | Stays offered |

The rules also cover:
- `submittedInTime` (art. 11a(5));
- the statement: name, order and email, each checked;
- the acknowledgement: content plus the date and time in UTC (art. 11a(4)), with no promise of a refund.

## Unit 1b: the buyer's function

**`/@store/orders`**
- One "Withdraw from contract here" link when any purchase is inside its period.
- It is one link rather than a line per purchase, because a line each would outgrow `ORDERS_PAGE_BYTES` (`orders-page-bounds` caught it).

**`/@store/orders/withdraw`**
- Without an order chosen, it lists the purchases inside their period, read and paid for as an opening of the list is (`openOrders`, then `purchasesFor`).
- With one chosen, it shows the product and the order, asks for a name, and fills in the email for the confirmation from the link's address (editable).
- The button is "Confirm withdrawal".
- Once the order is withdrawn from, or its period has passed, the page says so and offers no button.

**`POST /api/store/withdraw`** (plain form, works without JavaScript)
- The order must be one the link's address paid for (`findPurchase`, read again from Stripe).
- The statement is checked.
- The period is read at the moment of submission.
- It redirects with the outcome only; the name and email never go in the URL.

**`lib/withdrawal.ts`**
- Records the order once (`HSETNX`): the first statement's time, how many times its acknowledgement was tried, and whether it went. The record is counted in the store's data room first and kept 400 days. No name or email is kept.
- Emails the acknowledgement in the store's language, from "Store via Marktmorgen".
- If that email did not go, the next statement for the same order sends it again, with the first statement's time. It stops when one goes or after `WITHDRAWAL_ACK_SENDS` (3) tries for that order; each try is counted before it is made.

title: Costs: every picture upload's Blob operations and reads, under the owner's US$ 66 ceiling
body:
**The owner decided on 6 November 2026 (C4-20261106-2640-DONO-156):** the ceiling for a refunded first year on Creator goes from US$ 65 to **US$ 66**. It is an internal risk ceiling only: no price, visible limit or commission changes. This PR is no longer a draft.

## What it counts
Every picture upload uses Vercel Blob operations and reads that were never counted. This covers a product's picture, a link's picture and a page's picture. Each copy is put through its own upload request, and attaching the copies is one more request. Every one of these is a studio request (`studioAccess` → `countStudio`), capped hard at the plan's studio figure each month.

The new line `picture-uploads` in `tests/plan-cost-registry.ts` counts each request at its dearest:
- **11 puts**, Advanced Operations at US$ 5 per million: the put and every try again the Blob SDK may send (`BLOB_PUT_TRIES` = 1 + `VERCEL_BLOB_RETRIES`, 10 unless set);
- **3 × 11 + 2 Simple Operations** at US$ 0.40 per million: three heads (the one that checks a name is free, then one for the picture and one for its smaller copy), each with its tries again (`BLOB_HEAD_TRIES`, heads go through the same retrying request), and two reads, each a plain fetch sent once;
- both copies' whole bytes (`MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` each), at the dearer Blob transfer rate the registry already keeps.

Formula per tier: `studio × (11 × 5e-6 + (3 × 11 + 2) × 0.4e-6 + 2 × MAX_IMAGE_BYTES × 0.1e-9)`.

Prices come from vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing, read on 6 November 2026 by Claude 4 (C4-20261106-0830-C5-39).

## Why the read is counted whole
`firstBytes` (`lib/uploaded-image.ts`) reads a stream and cancels it after 16 bytes. Claude 4 checked the official pages on 6 November 2026: none says the Blob honors a byte range with 206, or bills only the bytes actually sent. The SDK's `get()` documents only 200 and 304. An unknown cost is never zero, so the whole file is counted.

## The result

| | Before | With this line |
|---|---|---|
| Store monthly usage | $6.93 | $7.47 |
| Refunded first year, Creator | $64.9688 | **$65.5068**, with every put and head try counted ($0.538 a month on Creator). Under the owner's US$ 66 |

Every unit is still positive (`docs/margin-alignment-2026-10-18.md` and the value presentation's rows are regenerated).

## The ceiling change (f11fd8a9)
- **`tests/plan-margin.test.ts`, test 30:** `year < 66`, with the decision cited.
- **`tests/read-ceilings.test.ts`, rule 23, annotated:** the day's heavy readings (2) were sized as the most that fit under US$ 65 (inbox C4-33). The extra dollar is room for this upload line, not for more readings, so the test now says exactly that:
  - the year, with the upload line, stays under US$ 66;
  - without the upload line, the year is under US$ 65 and one more heavy reading a day would still pass US$ 65.
  The figures when this test was annotated: year $65.3828 and upload line $0.414 (one put a request, before the retries were counted; the test reads the line from the code, so it holds with the current $0.538), one more reading $0.1007.
- **Rule 30:** the comments in `lib/calendar-limits.ts` and `lib/store-reading-rules.ts`, which said "the most the refund allows (US$ 65)", now say the figure was sized under US$ 65 and the US$ 66 is room for picture uploads. Comments only.
- `tests/picture-upload-costs.test.ts`: the header now cites the decision.

title: Encanto 5b-2: a ~240 px thumbnail copy at upload, checked like the smaller copy, its cost written down (stacked on #2790)
body:
Encanto unit 5b, second part. Claude 4 approved 5b with five conditions (C4-20261106-0700-C5-27) and supplied the official Blob prices (C4-20261106-0830-C5-39). #2785, #2786 and #2790 are merged. **This PR is now stacked on #2803**, because with every retry counted the thumbnail line fits only under the owner's US$ 66 ceiling, which #2803 brings (C4-20261106-2640-DONO-156).

## What it does
- **A third copy for thumbnails.** `lib/product-image.ts` adds `THUMB_LONG_SIDE` (240 px) and `MAX_THUMB_BYTES` (40 kB). This copy is for the 56 px pictures in lists, which take up to 2× on a sharp screen.
- **Read back only in its exact shape.** `ProductImage.thumb` is accepted only when it:
  - sits in the same folder;
  - is neither the picture nor its smaller copy;
  - is narrower than the copy above it;
  - stays within the byte ceiling.
- **Goes with the picture.** `imagePaths` includes the thumbnail, so it is replaced, deleted and copied to the pictures' bucket together with the picture.
- **Offered to the browser.** `smallerCopies` feeds both srcsets (`imageSrcSet`, `servedSrcSet`), narrowest first. A picture under 800 px that has a thumbnail now gets a srcset as well.
- **The editor** shrinks and uploads the thumbnail exactly like the smaller copy and sends it with the picture. A thumbnail that cannot be made or sent is left out.
- **The attach route:**
  - takes the thumbnail from the picture door together with the other copies;
  - names it in every `dropFresh`;
  - checks it as the smaller copy is checked: owned name; fresh, or the product's own; size from `head` within `MAX_THUMB_BYTES`; sniffed type matching the stored type; narrower than the copy above.

  A thumbnail that fails is dropped and never written.

## The five conditions

| Condition | How it is met |
|---|---|
| (1) Same checks as the smaller copy; invalid refused without writing | Same door, ownership, `head`, `firstBytes` sniff and type match, plus a fixed byte ceiling and a narrower width. A failing copy is dropped (`dropFresh`) and never recorded. |
| (2) Bytes counted in the storage meter | **Not met; corrected on 6 November 2026.** This row said the thumbnail is in the store's picture folder and that `storageUsed` measures it. That is wrong: `storageUsed` (`lib/storage-quota.ts` → `filesHeld`, `lib/file-store.ts:138`) lists only `stores/<folder>/`, and every picture copy, this thumbnail included, is kept under `images/<folder>/`. What is true: the thumbnail goes with the picture through `imagePaths` (replaced, deleted and copied with it); each one comes through its own door request (a studio request), so it adds at most `MAX_THUMB_BYTES` (40 kB) per product picture: 2,000 products × 40 kB = 80 MB ≈ US$ 0.0018 a month at US$ 0.023 per GB. The storage of `images/` as a whole is outside any meter and any cost line; reported to Claude 4 in the external-cost audit, to be decided before this merges. |
| (3) Cost recorded, worst case per plan, source and date | New line `picture-thumbnails` in `tests/plan-cost-registry.ts`. Its formula is below. Prices: vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing, read 6 November 2026. |
| (4) Old pictures untouched; no batch reprocessing | Pictures from before have no thumbnail and are served exactly as before. Nothing is reprocessed. |
| (5) Background only | Not applicable to the copy. The color part is #2790 (merged). |

For condition (3), every thumbnail goes through its own upload request. That request is a studio request (`studioAccess` → `countStudio`), capped hard at the plan's studio figure each month. The line counts each request at its dearest:
- its put at US$ 5 per million, with every retry the Blob SDK may send: `BLOB_PUT_TRIES` = 11 (Revisor 1 on #2803; rule 30);
- two heads at US$ 0.40 per million, for its name and for the thumbnail when attached, each with its retries (`BLOB_HEAD_TRIES` = 11, because `head()` goes through the SDK's `requestApi`);
- one read, a plain `fetch` through `get()` sent once (Codex S on #2801);
- its whole bytes, at the dearer Blob transfer rate the registry already keeps.

title: 648 [WG8]: an honest message for each state back from the checkout
body:
Queue item 648 [WG8] (C4-20261105-2125-C5-7, decisions C4-20261105-2130-C5-8). The VR rule applies: text a buyer reads about a charge. **Two independent reviews**. Codex A3 reviews first the single agreed line in `lib/store-checkout.ts`.

## Defect

Back from the checkout without a settled payment, every session that was open or expired came back from `readOrder` as `{ state: "unpaid" }`. The page then told the buyer "If you closed the payment page before finishing, **nothing was charged**", with no proof. That includes:
- a PaymentIntent that succeeded while the session was still open;
- a subscription already made;
- an answer in another shape.

There was no text for a declined card, nor for a payment still being checked.

## Fix (head `83dcd105`)

- **`lib/checkout-return.ts` (new, pure):** `unpaidProof(session)` reads only the session `readOrder` already fetched, which already expands `payment_intent.latest_charge` and `subscription`. No new Stripe call. It returns:
  - **`none`:** proof that nothing was charged. The session is open or expired and unpaid, with no subscription made. Its PaymentIntent is absent, canceled, or waiting for a payment method with no error. It has no charge, or only a failed, unpaid one.
  - **`declined`:** the PaymentIntent waits for a payment method after an error, with no charge or only a failed one.
  - **`checking`:** everything else. That includes a PaymentIntent that is succeeded, processing, requires_capture, requires_action or in an unknown status, a charge that went through, unexpanded or odd fields, getters, inherited fields and non-objects.
- **`lib/store-checkout.ts`:** the one agreed line. `readOrder` returns `{ state: "unpaid", proof: unpaidProof(session) }`, and the `Order` type carries the proof. No PR open at the time touched lines 1006–1012.
- **`app/[handle]/thanks/page.tsx`:**
  - An unpaid order's notice is chosen by its proof.
  - The notice body is `role="status"`.
- **`lib/buyer-words/thanks.ts`, all 7 buyer languages:**
  - **unpaid (proof):** "You were not charged".
  - **declined:** "Your payment did not go through", saying nothing was charged and the buyer can pay another way.
  - **checking (new):** "We are checking your payment. Do not pay again. If it went through, your confirmation email comes within a few minutes, and this page shows your order when you open it again."
  - **processing:** the text of before, plus "Do not pay again."

**Changed from the item's text (Claude 4, C4-20261105-2130-C5-8):** the item asked for "We will email you" for a payment that settles later and for a payment still being checked. The checkout sweep (`lib/checkout-sweep.ts`) reads only the last day of checkouts, so a payment that clears after a day has no email guaranteed. The page therefore promises none.
